# FDG8060

> DO NOT use `Nullable<T>` unless you would use a reference type in a similar manner, taking advantage of the fact that reference type values can be null.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.8 Nullable&lt;T>.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: draft

Analyzer candidate rejected: a nullable parameter, as in the bad Foo constructor, can stand for a value that is not available rather than an optional argument, and the text allows Nullable<T> wherever a reference type would use null in the same way.

## From the book

For example, you would not use null to represent optional parameters.

```csharp
// bad design
public class Foo {
  public Foo(string name, int? id);
}
// good design
public class Foo {
  public Foo(string name, int id);
  public Foo(string name);
}
```
